name: android-tools
description: adb-based tools for Android development, written in Rust.

requirements.device: Connected Android device or emulator with USB debugging authorized

tools.name: adbkit
tools.description: Shared adb helpers for the android-tools workspace
tools.long_description: Library crate with device picking and listing, shell/exec-out wrappers with timeouts, the uiautomator hierarchy model (XML to flat nodes, via roxmltree), density parsing (wm density) and pure helpers. Tool-specific behaviour stays in the tools that own it.
features: Serial auto-pick when a single device is connected
list_serials for tools that act on every connected device
shell_opt for commands whose failure is a normal outcome
shell_timeout with hard kill (uiautomator dump hangs)
exec_out for raw stdout (screencap)
resolve_launcher: a package's launcher activity, shared by uitool, startperf and appctl
uiautomator hierarchy parsing shared by the UI tools (roxmltree, testable without a device)
wm density parsing for px↔dp conversion (override wins over physical)

tools.name: appctl
tools.description: App lifecycle over adb — clear data/cache, restart, kill, uninstall, deep links, one or every device
tools.long_description: Runs the app-lifecycle actions IntelliJ's adb-idea puts behind a click, from the command line: clear data (pm clear) or cache only (pm trim-caches 0 — the Storage "clear cached data" path; pm clear --cache-only stalls on some builds), force-stop, restart (force-stop then relaunch on the launcher activity resolved at run time), uninstall, open the app's Settings page, and open a deep link. Acts on one device, several -s serials, or every connected device at once (--all); one line per device, [serial] prefix when there are several, exit 1 if any failed after every device was tried. Package names and URIs are validated instead of interpolated, so shell metacharacters never reach the device shell, and every device command has a 10s deadline so a stalled adb shell errors instead of hanging.

requires.device: Connected device/emulator with USB debugging authorized

features: 7 actions: clear-data, clear-cache (pm trim-caches), kill, restart, uninstall, Settings page, open deep link
--all runs on every connected device, -s is repeatable: one line per device
Restart resolves the launcher activity at run time (no hardcoded .MainActivity)
Package names and URIs validated, never interpolated into the device shell
Every device command has a 10s deadline: a stalled adb shell errors instead of hanging
Exit 1 if any device failed, after every device was tried

tools.name: assetgen
tools.description: Android density asset generator — launcher, notification, adaptive, 9-patch from one source PNG
tools.long_description: Offline Android Asset Studio: turns one square source PNG into the full density set (mdpi to xxxhdpi) — legacy launcher icons with optional circle-cropped round variants, notification icons, generic drawables at any dp base, adaptive icons (108 dp foreground/background layers plus the mipmap-anydpi-v26 entries) and validated .9.png rescales that keep markers 1 px wide and moving with their content. Lanczos3 scaling, platform dp rounding, no device and no SDK.
features: Launcher icons (mipmap-*, 48 dp) with --round circle crop
Notification icons (drawable-*, 24 dp)
Generic drawables at any --dp base
Adaptive icons: 108 dp layers + mipmap-anydpi-v26 XMLs, color or PNG background
9-patch rescale across densities with aapt-contract validation
Lanczos3 scaling, platform rounding, warnings before upscaling

tools.name: dpx
tools.description: px ↔ dp ↔ sp converter — offline, or against the device's real density
tools.long_description: Converts Android dimensions between px, dp and sp from the command line. Offline by default (any density value works, mdpi 160 dpi as the baseline), or --device reads the real density from the connected device via wm density, override winning over physical — that is what the UI actually draws at. Takes several values at once, one result per line, and honours a custom font scale for sp.

requires.adb: only for --device mode: Android SDK platform-tools in PATH

features: px ↔ dp ↔ sp in any direction (px = dp × density / 160, sp scales with the font scale)
--device reads the real density from wm density (override wins over physical)
Several values per call, one result per line
Pure conversion core, fully tested without a device

tools.name: layoutlint
tools.description: UI hierarchy lint — touch targets, overlap, labels, from a uiautomator dump
tools.long_description: Lints a uiautomator UI hierarchy for the defects scripts and users trip over: tap targets under 48 dp, two targets stacked on each other, clickable views with no visible label, and labels sitting on nodes that are not tappable while an identical clickable one exists. Reads the dump from a connected device or replays a saved file (no device needed for CI), converts px to dp using the device density, and gates on exit codes: text or JSON report, exit 1 on any finding, --warn-only to opt out.

requires.adb: only for --device mode: Android SDK platform-tools in PATH

features: Four rules: undersized touch targets (< 48 dp), overlapping tap targets, unlabeled clickable views, duplicated labels on non-tappable nodes
--device dumps the connected device; --xml replays a saved dump with no device at all (CI)
px→dp using the real screen density (`wm density`, override wins)
Text and JSON reports; exit 1 on any finding for CI, --warn-only to keep exit 0
--min-touch tunes the 48 dp guidance

tools.name: logstream
tools.description: Live Android log streamer - logcat, but actually nice
tools.long_description: Streams `adb logcat` (threadtime, main/system/crash buffers) filtered to one app package, with a ratatui TUI (search, level/tag filters, pid tracking, crash and restart banners) plus plain and JSONL output modes for piping.
features: App-pid filtering with crash history kept across restarts
Auto package resolution (tries <pkg> then <pkg>.debug)
Crash / start / restart / died banners (AndroidRuntime FATAL EXCEPTION detection)
Stack-trace continuation lines merged into the record
Live TUI with regex search, level and tag filters
JSONL and plain modes for scripts, optional file mirror

tools.name: perfpoll
tools.description: Per-app performance sampler over adb — CPU, RAM, battery drain, fps to CSV/JSON
tools.long_description: Polls one or more Android apps on a fixed interval over adb and streams one row per app per tick: CPU share (/proc/stat + /proc/pid/stat deltas), RAM (dumpsys meminfo PSS), battery (global level plus per-app cumulative mAh deltas from dumpsys batterystats) and frame stats (dumpsys gfxinfo Total/Janky deltas over real elapsed time). Writes CSV as it goes (safe to Ctrl+C) or one JSON document with per-app summaries at the end.
features: Multi-package sampling: -p repeatable, one CSV series with an app column
CPU% from /proc deltas across all of an app's pids, clamped to 0..100
RAM as the sum of per-process PSS TOTAL rows of dumpsys meminfo
Battery as global level plus per-app mAh deltas (UID / uid / package spellings)
FPS and janky-frame rate from gfxinfo counter deltas over actual elapsed time
Streamed CSV flushed per row (Ctrl+C-safe) or one pretty JSON document with summaries

tools.name: resclean
tools.description: Dead res/ resource detector for Android projects — CI gate
tools.long_description: Finds resources an Android project defines but never uses: walks res/ files and values entries, cross-references them against layouts, menus, manifests, other res/ XML and Kotlin/Java code (R.* / R2.*), and reports the dead ones as text or JSON. Pure source scan — no device, no aapt, no Gradle — with an exit-1 CI gate and --keep patterns for dynamically reached (getIdentifier) resources.
features: Scans res/ files and values/*.xml for definitions; layouts, menus, manifests, res/ XML and R.*/R2.* code for references
Qualifier- and .9.png-normalized keys; @+id/ defines an id (unused ids are reported), @id/ and R.id. reference one
Style names matched across code and XML (R.style.Theme_X = @style/Theme.X)
tools: preview attributes count as used; attr never reported; getIdentifier() handled via --keep patterns
Text and JSON reports; exit 1 on any dead resource for CI, --warn-only to opt out

tools.name: scenediff
tools.description: Visual regression diff of two screenshots, files or device captures
tools.long_description: Visual regression testing from the command line: compares two screenshots pixel by pixel (files, or two live captures from a device), reports how many pixels differ, in what percentage and where (bounding box), and writes a red-marked overlay image. A --threshold percentage turns the comparison into a CI gate.

requires.adb: only for --device mode: Android SDK platform-tools in PATH

features: Compares image files, or two live screencap captures (--device)
Euclidean RGB pixel comparison: count, percentage and bounding box of what changed
Red overlay image: every differing pixel plus a two-pixel frame around the bbox
--threshold % turns the diff into a CI gate (exit 1 strictly above it)
--region x1,y1,x2,y2 crops both sides, ignoring e.g. the status bar or a clock
JSON report for machine consumers

tools.name: startperf
tools.description: App cold/warm start benchmark over adb
tools.long_description: Measures cold and warm app launch times without Android Studio: runs `am start -W` N times against an activity, parses the framework-reported timings (TotalTime/WaitTime/ThisTime), and summarizes them as min/median/mean/max/stddev. Reports as a table, JSON or CSV, and skips runs Android admits it did not really launch.
features: Cold mode force-stops before every run; warm mode presses HOME so the process stays alive and the activity is recreated
Runs where Android admits it launched nothing ("brought to the front" in cold mode, "top-most instance" anywhere) are skipped, not counted
min/median/mean/max/stddev — median reported because cold samples skew
JSON report and spreadsheet-ready CSV with one row per run
Launcher activity resolved automatically via adbkit (or pass --component)

tools.name: svg2vd
tools.description: SVG → Android VectorDrawable XML converter — pure, no device, no Android SDK
tools.long_description: Converts an SVG into an Android VectorDrawable XML (res/drawable/*.xml), deterministically and without an Android SDK: usvg parses the document, the emitter walks the tree and hand-writes the XML. Shapes become pathData (arcs arrive as cubics), fills carry the fill-opacity folded into the #AARRGGBB alpha byte and evenOdd fillType, strokes carry color/width/cap/join/miterlimit/dashes with renderer defaults omitted, and transforms are baked into the path coordinates so rotation and skew stay representable. Clipped groups emit <clip-path android:pathData>. Anything VectorDrawable cannot express is approximated and reported, never fatal: gradients fall back to their first stop color, group opacity and patterns are warned about, text and images are skipped. The first fully pure crate of the workspace: 12 tests, no device, no adb.
features: Shapes to pathData: rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path
Fills: solid color, fill-opacity folded into the #AARRGGBB alpha, evenOdd fillType
Strokes: color, width, cap, join, miterlimit, dasharray/offset — renderer defaults omitted
Transforms baked into the coordinates: rotation, skew and scale stay representable
clip-path: a clipped group becomes <group> with <clip-path android:pathData>
Gradients fall back to their first stop color, patterns to black — with a warning, never fatal
12 pure tests, no device: the first fully pure crate of the workspace

tools.name: uitool
tools.description: Practical Android UI driver — dump, find, tap, shot over adb
tools.long_description: Drives a device UI from the command line: dumps the uiautomator hierarchy as labeled lines, finds/waits for nodes by text or content-desc, taps by label or coordinates, swipes, takes cropped/scaled screenshots, picks the color under any point, launches activities, sends keys and text.

requires.screen_on: uiautomator dump fails on a locked/off screen

features: Label-based interaction: tap/find/wait use text or content-desc, no coordinates needed
Clickable nodes preferred as tap target, bounds center computed automatically
uiautomator dump with hard timeout (no hangs) and screen-off detection
Screenshot pipeline: crop, nearest upscale, max-dim resize, JPEG quality
Color picker at any point (uitool pick x y → #AARRGGBB)
Serial auto-pick when exactly one device is connected (via adbkit)
